title: Place Order (Stock Check, Framework-Free)
instructions: The original Django task is rebuilt on an in-memory `Store` (see `ecom/store.py`, read-only) with the same domain rules. Implement `OrderServiceImpl.place_order` in `ecom/services/order_service_impl.py` and `OrderController.place_order` in `ecom/controllers/order_controller.py`. Check the user, then the stock of every product (raise `UserNotFoundError`, `ProductNotFoundError`, `OutOfStockError`), then decrement inventory and create a `PLACED` order with its items. Failures must change nothing, and concurrent requests must never overbook, so do the check and the decrement inside `store.transaction()`.

evidence.label: A valid order is PLACED, has one item per product and decrements each inventory
An unknown user raises UserNotFoundError and creates nothing
More than the stock raises OutOfStockError, exactly the stock is allowed
A failure on a later product leaves every inventory and the order table untouched
A product with no inventory row raises OutOfStockError
The same product on several lines is checked against the stock as a total
20 concurrent single-unit orders against 10 in stock succeed exactly 10 times
Controller returns SUCCESS with the order, or FAILURE without raising
